language.label: Language
language.description: Applies only to this browser. French is the default.

chat.gifNeedKey: Giphy search needs an API key (Settings → Local). You can also paste a URL.
chat.locationReady: Send the radio GPS as a location pin.

messageList.deleteConfirm: This removes the message from this device. Other mesh nodes still have it.
messageList.noEchoes: No echoes yet — view message status
messageList.analyzeDescription: On-demand raw packet analysis for a message-backed archival packet.
messageList.analyzeNotice: This analyzer shows one stored full packet copy only. When multiple receives have identical payloads, the backend deduplicates them to a single stored packet and appends any additional receive paths onto the message path history instead of storing multiple full packet copies.
messageList.analyzeUnavailable: No archival raw packet is available for this message, so packet analysis cannot be shown.
messageList.analyzePurged: The archival raw packet for this message is no longer available. It may have been purged from Settings > Database, so only the stored message and merged route history remain.
messageList.analyzeLoadFailed: Could not load the archival raw packet for this message: {{description}}
messageList.observerReachCaveat: Nodes that published hearing this message to Meshloom Community:
messageList.observerReachEmpty: No node has published hearing this packet to Meshloom Community.
messageList.observerReachMapAria: Map of the nodes that heard this packet

settings.staleHelp: Off by default. When set, a background job deletes non-favorite contacts using the same last-heard-before filter as Bulk Delete. 0 disables the job.
settings.groupsHelp: Local labels for the sidebar. Groups are not synced to the radio.
settings.directoryViaStats: Meshloom Community is on, so hop names, locate, and heard-by counts come from Community. The browser never contacts Community directly; the server relays. 1-byte hops are never sent.
settings.backupKeyWarning: The radio private key is stored in memory only and is not in these downloads. Keep a separate radio key backup if you need one.
settings.backupDbHelp: Full snapshot of meshcore.db: mesh history, channel keys, VAPID keys, fanout configs (MQTT, webhooks, bots, SQS), and push subscriptions. Treat this file as a secret. The radio private key is the only thing missing (it lives in memory). Restore is operator-level: stop the server and replace the file yourself. This app will not overwrite the live database.
settings.backupJsonHelp: Contacts, channels, settings, and groups only. No messages, packets, or private key.
settings.restoreJsonHelp: Merges into the live database. Does not replace meshcore.db and does not delete messages, packets, or contacts missing from the file. Reload the page after restore.
settings.restoreConfirm: I understand this merges into the live database
settings.restoreMergedDetail: {{contacts}} contacts, {{channels}} channels, {{groups}} groups. Reload the page.
settings.giphyKeyHelp: Optional. Used only for GIF picker search. Create a free beta key at developers.giphy.com. Incoming GIFs render without a key (they load from media.giphy.com).

local.deviceOnly: These settings apply only to this device/browser.
local.localLabelHelp: Display a colored banner at the top of the page to identify this instance.
local.distanceUnitsHelp: Controls how distances are shown throughout the app.
local.reopenLastHelp: Automatically reopen to the last-open channel or contact when the app loads to the bare URL.
local.autoFocusHelp: Place the cursor in the message input when switching conversations. Desktop only.
local.batteryPercentHelp: Display the radio's battery percentage in the status bar. Data updates every 60 seconds and may take up to a minute to appear after connecting.
local.batteryVoltageHelp: Display the radio's battery voltage in the status bar (in mV). Data updates every 60 seconds and may take up to a minute to appear after connecting.
local.statusDotPulseHelp: Flash the connection status dot in color as packets arrive: blue for channel, purple for DM, cyan for advert, green for other.
local.richPayloads: Render MeshCore Open reactions as emoji
local.richPayloadsHelp: MeshCore Open clients send emoji reactions as encoded text (e.g. r:1a2b:05). When enabled, unmatched reaction messages render as the emoji instead of the raw text. GIFs always display as images — they load from media.giphy.com, which reaches outside your local network and exposes your IP to Giphy.
local.pathHopWidthHelp: Append the per-hop identifier width to the hop-count badge on received messages — e.g. (2 · 2B) for a 2-hop path with 2-byte hops. Direct (0-hop) messages show no width.
local.textReplaceHelp: Automatically replace characters as you type in the message input. Define replacements as a JSON object mapping source strings to their replacements.
local.textReplaceUnsaved: {{error}} Changes are not saved until this is resolved.
local.fontSizeHelp: Scales the app's typography for this browser only. The slider moves in 5% steps; the number field accepts any value from 25% to 400%.

preview.intro: Preview alert, message, sidebar, and badge contrast for the selected theme.
preview.connected: Connected preview: radio link healthy and syncing.
preview.infoAlert: Info: channel slot cache refreshed from radio.
preview.errorAlert: Error: post-connect setup timed out. Reboot the radio and restart.

notifications.thisDeviceHelp: Receive notifications even when the browser is closed. Use the bell icon in a conversation header to override that contact or channel, or subscribe this browser to receive the defaults below.
notifications.thisDeviceGlobalHelp: Default rules and conversation exceptions are shared by every subscribed browser on this install. Subscribing or unsubscribing a browser only controls whether that browser receives them.
notifications.unsupported: Push notifications are not supported by this browser.
notifications.needsHttps: Web Push requires HTTPS. Access Meshloom over HTTPS (self-signed certificates work) to enable push notifications.
notifications.defaultsHelp: First-seen alerts fire after radio setup when a new companion, repeater, or sensor appears on the mesh. Unknown nodes and room servers never trigger a first-seen notification.
notifications.newContactHelp: Notify when a companion contact is first seen. Either this toggle or Companion advertisements is enough.
notifications.newDmHelp: Notify on incoming direct messages and room-server posts, unless a conversation exception overrides it.
notifications.advertRepeaterHelp: Notify when a repeater is first seen on the mesh.
notifications.advertCompanionHelp: Notify when a companion node is first seen. Either this toggle or New contacts is enough.
notifications.advertSensorHelp: Notify when a sensor is first seen on the mesh.
notifications.channelFoundHelp: Notify when a new hashtag channel is found. Conversation exceptions do not apply.
notifications.telemetryAlertHelp: Notify when a tracked telemetry reading raises an alert. Conversation exceptions do not apply.
notifications.exceptionsHelp: Per-conversation overrides set from a chat header. They take precedence over the defaults above.
notifications.vapidSubjectHelp: VAPID contact: mailto:you@domain.tld (recommended) or https://your-host with no path. Empty uses the server environment fallback. Apple rejects .local addresses.
notifications.vapidSubjectInvalid: Must be empty, a mailto:you@domain.tld, or an https://host origin (no path).

radio.disconnectHelp: Disconnect pauses automatic reconnect attempts so another device can use the radio.
radio.compatWarningBody: ALL nodes along a message's route — your radio, every repeater, and the recipient — must be running firmware that supports the selected mode. Messages sent with 2-byte or 3-byte hops will be dropped by any node on older firmware.
radio.advertLocationHelp: Companion-radio firmware does not distinguish between saved coordinates and live GPS here. When enabled, adverts include the node's current location state. That may be the last coordinates you set from Meshloom or live GPS coordinates if the node itself is already updating them. Meshloom cannot enable GPS on the node through the interface library.
radio.telemetrySharingHelp: Controls what this radio shares when other nodes request its telemetry. “Deny” blocks all requests, “Per-Contact” uses per-contact permission flags on the radio, and “Allow All” shares with any requester.
radio.rebootHelp: Some settings may require a reboot to take effect on some radios.
radio.exportHelp: Export saves the current server config to a JSON file. Import loads a config file, applies it, and reboots the radio.
radio.multiAcksHelp: When enabled, the radio sends one extra direct ACK transmission before the normal ACK for received direct messages. This is a firmware-level receive behavior, not a Meshloom retry setting.
radio.autoResendHelp: When enabled, outgoing channel messages that receive no echo within 2 seconds are automatically resent once (byte-perfect, within the 30-second dedup window). Repeaters that already heard the original will ignore the duplicate. This functionality will NOT create double-sent/duplicate messages.
radio.floodScopeHelp: Tag outgoing messages with a region name (e.g. MyRegion). Repeaters configured for that region can forward the traffic, while repeaters configured to deny other regions may drop it. Leave empty to send unscoped (plain flood). Forcing unscoped when a default scope is configured on the radio requires firmware v12 or newer. Individual channels can override this with their own region or an "always unscoped" setting.
radio.knownRegionsHelp: One region name per line. Incoming region-scoped (TransportFlood/TransportDirect) packets are matched against this list so messages and the packet inspector show a readable region label instead of a raw transport code. Saving a change re-tags existing messages whose original packet is still stored.
radio.discoverRegionsHelp: Asks nearby repeaters which regions they flood, so you can populate the list above. Uses repeaters from your last mesh discovery sweep when available, otherwise your most recently seen repeaters. Only repeaters in direct range answer, and this only reveals flood-allowed regions (not blocked ones).
radio.maxContactsHelp: Configured radio contact capacity. Favorites reload first, then background maintenance refills to about 80% of this value and offloads once occupancy reaches about 95%.
radio.maxContactsWarn: Your radio reports a hardware limit of {{max}} contacts. The effective cap will be limited to what the radio supports.
radio.advertIntervalHelp: How often to automatically advertise presence. Set to 0 to disable. Minimum: 1 hour. Recommended: 24 hours or higher.
radio.sendAdvertHelp: Flood adverts propagate through repeaters. Zero-hop adverts are local-only and use less airtime.
radio.meshDiscoveryHelp: Discover nearby node types that currently respond to mesh discovery requests: repeaters and sensors.
radio.noNodesResponded: No supported nodes responded during the last discovery sweep.
radio.heardHere: Heard here: {{snr}} dB SNR / {{rssi}} dBm RSSI. Remote heard us: {{remote}} dB SNR.
radio.importKeyBody: This config file contains a private key. Importing it will change your radio's identity — your radio will have a new public key and other nodes will see it as a different device. This cannot be undone without the original key.
radio.geoUnsupportedHelp: Your browser does not support geolocation
radio.numericRequired: All numeric fields must have valid values
radio.regionsAlreadyListed: All discovered regions are already listed
radio.regionsAdded_one: Added {{count}} region — review and Save Messaging Settings
radio.regionsAdded_other: Added {{count}} regions — review and Save Messaging Settings
radio.exportWithoutKeyHelp: See README_ADVANCED.md for private key export enable
radio.invalidConfigHelp: File must contain name and radio parameters (freq, bw, sf, cr)
radio.importKeyRebooting: Config + private key imported, saving & rebooting...
radio.connectionChangeFailed: Failed to change radio connection state
radio.connectionChangeFailedHelp: Check radio connection and try again

radioApp.trackedRepeatersHelp: Repeaters opted into automatic telemetry collection are polled on a scheduled interval. To limit mesh traffic, the app caps telemetry at 24 checks per day across all tracked repeaters — so fewer tracked repeaters allows shorter intervals, and more tracked repeaters forces longer ones. Up to {{max}} repeaters may be tracked at once ({{used}} / {{max}} slots used).
radioApp.alertRulesHelp: Alerts apply only to tracked nodes. A threshold is checked only when a poll returns a usable value.
radioApp.batteryVoltsMinHelp: Alert when reported battery is below this voltage.
radioApp.noiseFloorMaxHelp: Alert when reported noise floor is above this level.
radioApp.missesBeforeAlertHelp: Alert after this many polls with no usable reply. This is not a second hour setting.
radioApp.intervalClamped_one: Saved preference is {{preferred}} hour, but the scheduler is using {{effective}} hours because {{tracked}} repeater is tracked. Your preference will be restored if you drop back to a supported count.
radioApp.intervalClamped_other: Saved preference is {{preferred}} hours, but the scheduler is using {{effective}} hours because {{tracked}} repeaters are tracked. Your preference will be restored if you drop back to a supported count.
radioApp.pollRoutedHourlyHelp: When enabled, tracked repeaters with a direct or routed path (not flood) are polled every hour instead of on the scheduled interval above. Flood-only repeaters still follow the normal schedule.
radioApp.nextFloodRun: Next flood run at {{time}} (UTC top of hour).
radioApp.nextRun: Next run at {{time}} (UTC top of hour).
radioApp.nextRoutedRun: Next direct/routed run at {{time}} (UTC top of hour).
radioApp.noRepeatersTracked: No repeaters are being tracked. Enable tracking from a repeater's dashboard.
radioApp.trackedContactsHelp: Non-repeater contacts (companions, rooms, sensors) can also be tracked for periodic LPP telemetry collection (battery, sensors, GPS). Up to 8 contacts may be tracked. The daily check ceiling is shared with tracked repeaters — adding contacts may clamp the interval upward.
radioApp.noContactsTracked: No contacts are being tracked. Enable tracking from a contact's info pane.
radioApp.blockDiscovery: Block Discovery of New Node Types
radioApp.blockDiscoveryHelp: Checked types will be ignored when heard via advertisement. Existing contacts of these types are still updated. This does not affect contacts added manually or via DM.
radioApp.blockedTypesWarn: New {{types}} heard via advertisement will not be added to your contact list.
radioApp.blockedContactsHelp: Blocked contacts are hidden from the sidebar. Blocking only hides messages from the UI — MQTT forwarding and bot responses are not affected. Messages are still stored and will reappear if unblocked.
radioApp.noBlocked: No blocked contacts. Block contacts from their info pane, viewed by clicking their avatar in any channel, or their name within the top status bar with the conversation open.
radioApp.bulkDeleteHelp: Remove multiple contacts or repeaters at once. Useful for cleaning up spam or unwanted nodes. Message history will be preserved.

bulk.title: Bulk Delete Contacts
bulk.selectHelp: Select contacts to delete. Message history will be preserved and accessible if a contact is re-added, but will no longer appear in the sidebar.
bulk.confirmHelp: Review the contacts that will be permanently deleted.
bulk.noMatch: No contacts match the selected filters.
bulk.name: Name
bulk.confirmDelete: I confirm permanent, irrevocable deletion of all listed nodes above, totalling {{summary}}, spanning creation dates from {{minDate}} to {{maxDate}}

database.deleteUndecryptedHelp: Permanently deletes stored raw packets that have not yet been decrypted. These are retained in case you later obtain the correct key — once deleted, these messages can never be recovered.
database.purgeArchivalHelp: Deletes the raw packet bytes behind messages that are already decrypted and visible in chat. This frees space but removes packet-analysis availability for those messages. It does not affect displayed messages or future decryption.
database.autoDecrypt: Auto-decrypt historical DMs when new contact advertises
database.autoDecryptHelp: When enabled, the server will automatically try to decrypt stored DM packets when a new contact sends an advertisement. This may cause brief delays on large packet backlogs.
database.invalidRetentionHelp: Retention days must be at least 1
database.purgeFailed: Failed to purge decrypted raw packets

stats.loading: Loading statistics... this can take a while if you have a lot of stored packets.
stats.pathHashHelp: Parsed stored raw packets from the last 24 hours: {{count}}
stats.noPathData: No path data in the last 24 hours.
stats.regionScopeHelp: How much local traffic uses regional flood scoping. Traffic covers all channel messages heard, including channels you have no key for; senders only counts channels you can decrypt, so the two use different denominators and will not match.
stats.floorNoise: Scoped message count is at or below the estimated false-positive floor ({{floor}}) from corrupt packet captures, so it is not evidence of regional adoption.
stats.floorIncludes: Includes an estimated {{floor}} false positives from corrupt packet captures.
stats.senderUnaffected: The sender count is unaffected — it requires successful decryption.
stats.noChannelMessages: No channel messages heard in the last 24 hours.
stats.noNoiseSamples: No noise floor samples collected yet. Samples are collected every minute and retained until server restart.
stats.oneNoiseSample: Only one sample so far ({{dbm}} dBm). More data needed for a chart. Samples are collected every minute and retained until server restart.

community.intro: Meshloom Community is on by default. Enter the IATA code of the nearest airport so this server can publish overheard packets and use the community directory. The browser talks only to this Meshloom server.
community.joinHelp: Turn Meshloom Community back on and save a 3-letter IATA airport code. Nothing is published until you join.
community.bannerMessage: To use all Meshloom Community features, enter the IATA code of the nearest airport.
community.bannerOptedOut: Meshloom Community is off. Turn it on and enter the IATA code of the nearest airport to use all community features.
community.enableHelp: When off, this server does not publish to Meshloom Community.
community.disableHelp: Stopping Meshloom Community stops publish, and also stops the online directory: no hop names, no locate anchors, no heard-by counts.
community.locked: The operator locked Meshloom Community. Enable is disabled.
community.lockedEnable: Meshloom Community enable is locked by the operator.
community.iataHelp: The IATA code is the 3-letter code of the nearest airport (A–Z). It is a coarse region label. Concordance only means it is consistent with your radio position — never a verified location.
community.iataInvalid: IATA must be exactly 3 letters A–Z.
community.noIataPublishOff: No IATA code is saved, so publish stays off.
community.iataChangeCap: IATA change cap reached. Try again later.
community.overrideHelp: Confirm this IATA even if it is not consistent with your radio position. This confirmation is not change-capped.
community.concordanceOk: This IATA is consistent with your radio position.
community.concordanceWarn: This IATA is only loosely consistent with your radio position.
community.concordanceMismatch: This IATA is not consistent with your radio position.
community.concordanceUnknown: Cannot compare this IATA with your radio position yet.
community.privacyAccount: Your radio public key is the account.
community.privacyPrivateKey: Anyone with the radio private key can publish and read your “me” stats.
community.privacyRotate: Rotating the radio key orphans your history and IATA bind.
community.privacyHashtags: When Community is on, Meshloom shares hashtag channel names — not messages or private keys — with your IATA zone so others can find public rooms.
community.privacyDirectory: With Community off there is no directory at all. Meshloom never contacts any other host.

about.madeBy: Made with love and open source by <author>Pascal M</author>
about.kofi: This code is free, and ad-free, forever. If you love my work, <kofi>buy me a coffee!</kofi>
about.thanks: With great appreciation to those who have made the tools upon which this is built:
about.updateAvailableHelp: This node is v{{current}}. Latest published release is v{{latest}}.

create.title: Create Integration
create.empty: No integration types are currently available.

mqtt_private.label: Private MQTT
mqtt_private.description: Customizable-scope forwarding of all or some messages to an MQTT broker of your choosing, in raw and/or decrypted form.

mqtt_ha.label: Home Assistant MQTT Discovery
mqtt_ha.description: Publishes MQTT Discovery payloads so mesh devices appear natively in Home Assistant. Requires HA's built-in MQTT integration connected to the same broker. Select specific contacts for GPS tracking and repeaters for telemetry sensors.

mqtt_community.label: Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt
mqtt_community.description: MeshcoreToMQTT-compatible raw-packet feed publishing, compatible with community aggregators (in other words, make your companion radio also serve as an observer node). Superset of other Community MQTT presets.

mqtt_community_meshrank.label: MeshRank
mqtt_community_meshrank.description: A community MQTT config preconfigured for MeshRank, requiring only the provided topic from your MeshRank configuration. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.

mqtt_community_letsmesh_us.label: LetsMesh (US)
mqtt_community_letsmesh_us.description: A community MQTT config preconfigured for the LetsMesh US-ingest endpoint, requiring only your email and IATA region code. Good to use with an additional EU configuration for redundancy. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.

mqtt_community_letsmesh_eu.label: LetsMesh (EU)
mqtt_community_letsmesh_eu.description: A community MQTT config preconfigured for the LetsMesh EU-ingest endpoint, requiring only your email and IATA region code. Good to use with an additional US configuration for redundancy. A subset of the primary Community MQTT/meshcoretomqtt configuration; you are free to edit all configuration after creation.

webhook.label: Webhook
webhook.description: Generic webhook for decrypted channel/DM messages with customizable verb, method, and optional HMAC signature.

apprise.label: Apprise
apprise.description: A wide-ranging generic fanout, capable of forwarding decrypted channel/DM messages to Discord, Telegram, email, SMS, and many others.

sqs.label: Amazon SQS
sqs.description: Send full or scope-customized raw or decrypted packets to an SQS

bot.label: Python Bot
bot.description: A simple, Python-based interface for basic bots that can respond to DM and channel messages.

map_upload.label: Map Upload
map_upload.description: Upload repeaters and room servers to map.meshcore.io or a compatible map API endpoint.

toast.missingId: Missing fanout config id for update

list.experimentalBanner: Integrations are an experimental feature in open beta, and allow you to fanout raw and decrypted messages across multiple services for automation, analysis, or archiving.
list.botsDisabled: Bot system is disabled by server configuration (MESHCORE_DISABLE_BOTS). Bot integrations cannot run, be created, or be modified.
list.botsDisabledUntilRestart: Bot system is disabled until the server restarts. Bot integrations cannot run, be created, or be modified right now.
list.name: Name
list.errorDescription: Most recent backend error retained for this integration.

mqtt.privateHelp: Forward mesh data to your own MQTT broker for home automation, logging, or alerting.
mqtt.outgoingWarning: Outgoing messages (DMs and group messages) will be reported to private MQTT brokers in decrypted/plaintext form.

ha.title: Home Assistant MQTT Discovery
ha.help: Publish discovery configs and MeshCore state to your MQTT broker so Home Assistant creates native devices, sensors, GPS trackers, and message events automatically.
ha.step1Help: Home Assistant's built-in MQTT integration must point at the same broker configured below.
ha.step2Help: Choose repeaters for telemetry sensors and contacts for GPS tracker entities.
ha.step3Help: Radio health and message events publish continuously; repeater and contact data update when new data is heard or collected.
ha.usesDiscovery: Uses <discovery>MQTT Discovery</discovery> and the topic conventions documented in <readme>README_HA.md</readme>.
ha.whatGetsCreated: What gets created in Home Assistant
ha.perRepeaterHelp: — updates on telemetry collect cycle (~8h) or manual dashboard fetch. Entity IDs shown use one repeater for example; these sensors are created for each selected repeater.
ha.perContactHelp: — updates passively when advertisements with GPS are heard, and from any GPS reading in the contact's CayenneLPP telemetry. Shown for one contact; a tracker is created for each selected contact.
ha.trackerHelp: — latitude/longitude (plus altitude when telemetry provides it)
ha.contactLpp: , etc. — CayenneLPP sensors (when the contact is tracked for telemetry; GPS goes to the tracker above)
ha.messageEventsFires: — fires for each message matching the scope below
ha.messageEventsTrigger: — trigger automations on sender, channel, or message content
ha.entityIdsHelp: Entity IDs use the first 12 characters of the node's public key. Entities are removed from HA when this integration is disabled or deleted. State topics are published under {{prefix}}/<node_id>/health|telemetry|gps.
ha.topicSummaryHelp: Home Assistant device and entity IDs are keyed off the first 12 characters of each node's public key, not the display name. Those same 12 characters are used in the MQTT state topics below.
ha.noTopicPreviews: No topic previews available yet. Connect to a radio to resolve the local radio key, and select contacts or repeaters above to preview their published topics.
ha.discoveryTopics: Discovery config topics are also published under homeassistant/.../config, but the topics above are the primary runtime state and event topics.
ha.topicPrefixHelp: State updates publish under {{prefix}}/. Discovery configs always use the homeassistant/ prefix.
ha.gpsHelp: Each selected contact becomes a device_tracker in HA, updated whenever an advertisement with GPS coordinates is heard. Useful for tracking mobile nodes on an HA map dashboard.
ha.telemetryHelp: Each selected repeater becomes an HA device with sensors for battery voltage, RSSI, SNR, noise floor, packet counts, and uptime. Data updates whenever telemetry is collected (auto-collect runs every ~8 hours, or on manual dashboard fetch). Only repeaters already in the auto-telemetry tracking list appear here (add new repeaters by logging into the repeater and opting in at the bottom of the page).
ha.noTrackedRepeaters: No repeaters are being auto-tracked for telemetry. Add repeaters to the auto-telemetry tracking list in the Radio section first, then return here to select which ones to expose to HA.
ha.trackedNotFound: Auto-tracked repeaters not found in contact list.
ha.messageEventsHelp: Matching messages fire an {{entity}} entity in HA with sender, text, channel, and direction attributes. Use HA automations to trigger actions on specific messages, channels, or contacts.

community.help: Advanced community MQTT editor. Use this for manual meshcoretomqtt-compatible setups or for modifying a saved preset after creation. Only raw RF packets are shared — never decrypted messages.
community.wsPathHelp: Defaults to / — use /mqtt for brokers that require a path
community.tokenAudienceHelp: Defaults to the broker host when blank
community.ownerEmailHelp: Used to claim your node on the community aggregator

meshrank.help: Pre-filled MeshRank setup. This saves as a regular Community MQTT integration once created, but only asks for the MeshRank packet topic you were given.
meshrank.brokerSummary: Broker {{host}} on port {{port}} via {{transport}}, auth {{auth}}, TLS on, certificate verification on, region code fixed to {{iata}}.
meshrank.topicHelp: Paste the full topic template from your MeshRank config, for example meshrank/uplink/B435F6D5F7896B74C6B995FE221C2C1F/{PUBLIC_KEY}/packets.

letsmesh.help: Pre-filled LetsMesh setup. This saves as a regular Community MQTT integration once created, but only asks for the values LetsMesh expects from you.
letsmesh.brokerSummary: Broker {{host}} on port {{port}} via {{transport}}, auth {{auth}}, TLS on, certificate verification on, token audience fixed to {{host}}.

bot.experimental: Experimental: This is an alpha feature and introduces automated message sending to your radio; unexpected behavior may occur. Use with caution, and please report any bugs!
bot.security: Security Warning: This feature executes arbitrary Python code on the server. Only run trusted code, and be cautious of arbitrary usage of message parameters.
bot.dontWreck: Don't wreck the mesh! Bots process ALL messages, including their own. Be careful of creating infinite loops!
bot.defineFunction: Define a bot() function that receives message data and optionally returns a reply.
bot.available: Available: Standard Python libraries and any modules installed in the server environment.
bot.note: Note: Bots respond to all messages, including your own. For channel messages, sender_key is None. Multiple enabled bots run concurrently. Outgoing messages are serialized with a two-second delay between sends to prevent repeater collision.

map.help: Automatically upload heard repeater and room server advertisements to map.meshcore.io. Requires the radio's private key to be available (firmware must have ENABLE_PRIVATE_KEY_EXPORT=1). Only raw RF packets are shared — never decrypted messages.
map.dryRunStatusOn: Dry Run is ON. No uploads will be sent. Check the backend logs to verify the payload looks correct before enabling live sends.
map.dryRunStatusOff: Dry Run is OFF. Live uploads are enabled. Each advert is rate-limited to once per hour per node.
map.dryRunHelp: When enabled, upload payloads are logged at INFO level but not sent. Disable once you have confirmed the logged output looks correct.
map.apiUrlHelp: Leave blank to use the default map.meshcore.io endpoint.
map.geofenceHelp: Only upload nodes whose location falls within the configured radius of your radio's own position. Helps exclude nodes with false or spoofed coordinates. Uses the latitude/longitude set in Radio Settings.
map.noCoords: Your radio does not currently have a latitude/longitude configured. Geofencing will be silently skipped until coordinates are set in Settings → Radio → Location.
map.usingPosition: Using radio position {{lat}}, {{lon}} as the geofence center. Update coordinates in Radio Settings to move the center.
map.radiusHelp: Nodes further than this distance from your radio's position will not be uploaded.

scope.title: Message Scope
scope.emptyWarning: Nothing is selected — this integration will not forward any data.
scope.onlyHint: Newly added channels or contacts will not be automatically included.
scope.exceptHint: Newly added channels or contacts will be automatically included unless excluded here.
scope.hidePills: >{{max}} selections made; hiding selection preview to keep the interface clean

apprise.help: Send push notifications via <apprise>Apprise</apprise> when messages are received. Supports Discord, Slack, Telegram, email, and <services>100+ other services</services>.
apprise.urlsHelp: One URL per line. All URLs receive every matched notification. For Matrix room version 12 (servername-less room IDs), append ?hsreq=no to the URL.
apprise.preserveIdentityHelp: When enabled, Discord webhooks will use their configured name/avatar instead of overriding with MeshCore sender info.
apprise.includeOutgoingHelp: Include DMs and channel messages sent by this Meshloom instance, including manual sends and bot replies. Outgoing messages carry no routing path or signal data, so path-related format fields render as direct and RSSI/SNR are empty.
apprise.markdownHelp: If notifications fail on services like Telegram due to special characters in sender names, disable this option.
apprise.varHopsBackticked: Hops wrapped in backticks for markdown
apprise.varsFooter: Empty textareas use the default format. RSSI/SNR may be empty if unavailable.

webhook.help: Send message data as JSON to an HTTP endpoint when messages are received.
webhook.hmacHelp: When a secret is set, each request includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the JSON body in the specified header (e.g. sha256=ab12cd...).

security.title: Unprotected bot execution is enabled
security.intro: Bots are not disabled, and app-wide Basic Auth is not configured.
security.networkRisk: Without one of those protections, or another access-control layer in front of Meshloom, anyone on your local network who can reach this app can run Python code on the computer hosting this instance via the bot system.
security.onlySafe: This is only safe on protected or isolated networks with appropriate access control. If your network is untrusted or later compromised, this setup may expose the host system to arbitrary code execution.
security.envHint: To reduce that risk, run the server with environment variables to either disable bots with <bots>MESHCORE_DISABLE_BOTS=true</bots> or enable the built-in login with <user>MESHCORE_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME</user> / <pass>MESHCORE_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD</pass>. Another external auth or access-control system is also acceptable.
security.temporary: If you just want a temporary safety measure while you learn the system, you can use the button below to disable bots until the server restarts. That is only a temporary guard; permanent protection through Basic Auth or env-based bot disablement is still encouraged.
security.acknowledge: I understand that continuing with my existing security setup may put me at risk on untrusted networks or if my home network is compromised.
security.dismiss: Do Not Warn Me On This Device Again

cracker.help: For unknown-keyed GroupText packets, this will attempt to dictionary attack, then brute force payloads as they arrive, testing channel names up to the specified length to discover active channels on the local mesh (GroupText packets may not be hashtag messages; we have no way of knowing but try as if they are). Retry failed at n+1 will return to the failed queue and pick up messages it couldn't find a key for, attempting them at one longer length. Try word pairs will also try every combination of two dictionary words concatenated together (e.g. "hello" + "world" = "#helloworld") after the single-word dictionary pass; this can substantially increase search time and also result in false-positives. Decrypt historical will run an async job on any channel name it finds to see if any historically captured packets will decrypt with that key. Turbo mode will push your GPU to the max (target dispatch time of 10s) and may allow accelerated searching and/or system instability.
